title: OSHA construction health hazards practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction health hazards practice questions on 29 CFR 1926 Subpart D: first aid, sanitation, noise, lasers, lighting, ventilation and lead.

questions.question: Under 1926.50(a), the employer must insure the availability of medical personnel for what purpose?

options.A: Advice and consultation on matters of occupational health
options.B: Signing each employee's weekly timesheet
options.C: Inspecting scaffolds before each shift
options.D: Approving the project's budget

questions.explanation: "The employer shall insure the availability of medical personnel for advice and consultation on matters of occupational health."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.50(d)(2), how must the contents of the first aid kit be packaged?

options.A: In a locked metal cabinet in the site office
options.B: In a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item
options.C: In any box marked with a red cross
options.D: In the glove box of a supervisor's vehicle

questions.explanation: "The contents of the first aid kit shall be placed in a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When must provisions be made for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury?

options.A: Within 24 hours after the first serious injury
options.B: When the project is half complete
options.C: Prior to commencement of the project
options.D: Only if the project lasts longer than 90 days

questions.explanation: "Provisions shall be made prior to commencement of the project for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, what must be conspicuously posted?

options.A: The OSHA area office address
options.B: The employer's insurance policy number
options.C: The list of first aid kit contents
options.D: The telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances

questions.explanation: "In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, the telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances shall be conspicuously posted."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: 911 service is available, and the employer contacts emergency medical service with a communication system that does not automatically give the dispatcher the caller's latitude and longitude. What must be posted conspicuously at the worksite?

options.A: The latitude and longitude of the worksite, or other location-identification information that communicates effectively to employees the location of the worksite
options.B: The employer's federal tax identification number
options.C: The telephone number of the OSHA area office
options.D: Nothing, because 911 is available

questions.explanation: The employer must post in a conspicuous location at the worksite either "The latitude and longitude of the worksite" or "Other location-identification information that communicates effectively to employees the location of the worksite."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: To whom do the toilet requirements of 1926.51(c) not apply?

options.A: Crews of 20 or fewer employees
options.B: Mobile crews having transportation readily available to nearby toilet facilities
options.C: Projects shorter than 30 days
options.D: Crews that work outdoors

questions.explanation: The requirements of paragraph (c) for sanitation facilities "shall not apply to mobile crews having transportation readily available to nearby toilet facilities."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must outlets for nonpotable water, such as water for industrial or firefighting purposes only, be identified under 1926.51(b)?

options.A: With blue paint on the pipe
options.B: With a padlock on the tap
options.C: By signs that indicate clearly the water is unsafe and is not to be used for drinking, washing, or cooking
options.D: With a red tap handle

questions.explanation: Such outlets "shall be identified by signs meeting the requirements of subpart G of this part, to indicate clearly that the water is unsafe and is not to be used for drinking, washing, or cooking purposes."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where showers are required by a particular standard, how many showers must be provided?

options.A: One per jobsite
options.B: One for each 40 employees
options.C: One for each 25 employees of each sex
options.D: One for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift

questions.explanation: "One shower shall be provided for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.51, Sanitation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.57(b), local exhaust systems must be designed so that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors or gases are handled in what way?

options.A: They are not drawn through the work area of employees
options.B: They are blown toward the nearest open window
options.C: They are drawn past the employees' breathing zone first
options.D: They are collected only at the end of each shift

questions.explanation: Local exhaust systems "shall be so designed that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors, or gases are not drawn through the work area of employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.57, Ventilation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.52(c), how is noise treated when its variations in level involve maxima at intervals of 1 second or less?

options.A: As impact noise limited to 140 dB
options.B: As continuous noise
options.C: As noise that is not counted
options.D: As noise measured on the C-scale

questions.explanation: "If the variations in noise level involve maxima at intervals of 1 second or less, it is to be considered continuous."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee's daily noise exposure is made up of periods at different levels, so the equivalent noise exposure factor Fe is computed. When does the exposure exceed permissible levels?

options.A: When Fe equals one half
options.B: When Fe is less than 1
options.C: When Fe exceeds unity (1)
options.D: Only when one period is above 115 dBA

questions.explanation: Fe is the sum of each period at a constant level divided by the permissible duration at that level, and "If the value of Fe exceeds unity (1) the exposure exceeds permissible levels."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.52(d)(1), what must be administered in all cases where the sound levels exceed the values shown in Table D-2?

options.A: A one-time hearing test at hire only
options.B: A written warning to each exposed employee
options.C: A monthly noise survey by OSHA
options.D: A continuing, effective hearing conservation program

questions.explanation: "In all cases where the sound levels exceed the values shown herein, a continuing, effective hearing conservation program shall be administered."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Section 1926.59 makes 1910.1200 the hazard communication rule for construction. Which of these does 1910.1200(b)(6) say the standard does not apply to?

options.A: Tobacco or tobacco products
options.B: Wood that may be sawed or cut later, generating dust
options.C: Chemicals contained in unlabeled pipes in work areas
options.D: Hazardous chemicals a subcontractor stores on site

questions.explanation: The construction requirements "are identical to those set forth at § 1910.1200 of this chapter", and 1910.1200 does not apply to "Tobacco or tobacco products". Wood "which may be subsequently sawed or cut, generating dust" is expressly not exempted.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1200, Hazard communication (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.62(j)(1)(ii), the employer must institute a medical surveillance program for employees who are or may be exposed at or above the action level for more than how long?

options.A: 1 day in any calendar year
options.B: 30 days in any consecutive 12 months
options.C: 90 days in any consecutive 6 months
options.D: 180 days in any consecutive 24 months

questions.explanation: The program is required "for all employees who are or may be exposed by the employer at or above the action level for more than 30 days in any consecutive 12 months". Separately, initial medical surveillance goes to "employees occupationally exposed on any day to lead at or above the action level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1926.54(h) require for laser systems when it is raining or snowing, or when there is dust or fog in the air?

options.A: They may be run at higher power to cut through the weather
options.B: Only the beam shutter needs to be closed between uses
options.C: Their operation is prohibited where practicable, and employees are kept out of range of the area of source and target
options.D: Nothing, because weather does not affect lasers

questions.explanation: In those conditions "the operation of laser systems shall be prohibited where practicable; in any event, employees shall be kept out of range of the area of source and target during such weather conditions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must be done when a laser is left unattended for a substantial period of time, such as during lunch hour or overnight?

options.A: Point it at the ground
options.B: Cover it with a tarp
options.C: Post a second warning placard
options.D: Turn the laser off

questions.explanation: "When the laser is left unattended for a substantial period of time, such as during lunch hour, overnight, or at change of shifts, the laser shall be turned off."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.55(b), equipment and technical measures used to keep exposure to air contaminants within the limits must first be approved for each particular use by whom?

options.A: A competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person
options.B: The equipment's sales representative
options.C: Any employee on the crew
options.D: The local fire marshal

questions.explanation: "Any equipment and technical measures used for this purpose must first be approved for each particular use by a competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For areas or operations not covered by Table D-3, where does 1926.56(b) refer the employer for recommended illumination values?

options.A: ANSI/ISEA Z87.1-2010
options.B: American National Standard A11.1-1965, R1970, Practice for Industrial Lighting

questions.explanation: For areas or operations not covered above, "refer to the American National Standard A11.1-1965, R1970, Practice for Industrial Lighting, for recommended values of illumination."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.56, Illumination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Respirators are used to limit employee exposure to lead, and all the requirements of 1926.62(e)(1) and (f) have been met. Under 1926.62(c)(3), how may employee exposure be considered for the periods the respirator is worn?

options.A: As zero for the whole shift, whatever respirator is used
options.B: At double the measured airborne level
options.C: At the level provided by the protection factor of the respirator
options.D: At half the PEL, whatever respirator is used

questions.explanation: In that case "employee exposure may be considered to be at the level provided by the protection factor of the respirator for those periods the respirator is worn." Those periods "may be averaged with exposure levels during periods when respirators are not worn to determine the employee's daily TWA exposure."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1926.62 define the action level for lead?

options.A: Any detectable lead in a blood sample
options.B: 50 µg/m3 measured inside the respirator
options.C: Any visible lead dust on a surface
options.D: Employee exposure, without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of 30 µg/m3 calculated as an 8-hour TWA

questions.explanation: Action level means employee exposure, "without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of lead of 30 micrograms per cubic meter of air (30 µg/m3) calculated as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.62, Lead (as of Nov 3, 2026)
